Expose Parquet files as a database of views

Source: R/connect.R
parquet_connect.Rd

Creates an in-memory DuckDB connection with one view per Parquet file (or per directory of Parquet files, for partitioned tables), so that every other function in the package works on a Parquet store exactly as on a database. Requires the duckdb package.

Usage

parquet_connect(path, union_by_name = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

path

A directory, or one or more .parquet files.

union_by_name

Pass union_by_name = true to read_parquet() so partitions with evolving columns still load.

...

Passed to DBI::dbConnect() for duckdb.

Value

A duckdb_connection. Disconnect with DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE).

Details

Given a directory, files are found recursively. Each directory becomes a schema (nested paths joined with _; files at the root go in main). A directory that holds two or more Parquet files, no subdirectories, and whose files all share one column schema is read as a single partitioned table named after the directory, so layer1/pas_adt_events/fy2022.parquet and fy2023.parquet become the view layer1.pas_adt_events. A directory whose files differ in schema is a schema of separate tables.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- parquet_connect("data/v2/sample")
db_tables(con)
inv <- db_inventory(con)
} # }
